c3.reason: Criterion not met after its one recheck: the worst-case pre-check bounds tokens by characters, which Unicode-heavy prompts can exceed. Spend is still capped by actual charges and the OpenRouter key credit limit.
c3.fix: Bound tokens by UTF-8 bytes (or a tokenizer upper bound) instead of characters in pricing.py; first task of PR2.

r1.reason: Recheck finding introduced by the binding fix: HAVING thresholds are cast to the column type, so count > 1.5 becomes > 2 on Postgres.
r1.fix: Bind HAVING/aggregate comparison values with the aggregate's result type (numeric for avg/sum, no integer cast for fractional thresholds); first task of PR2 with a cross-engine test.

r2.reason: Recheck finding: SQLite date-vs-datetime normalization truncates to milliseconds, so a timestamp microseconds after midnight compares equal to the date.
r2.fix: Use '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%f' plus a microsecond-preserving comparison (or julianday with exact text fallback) and add a sub-millisecond test; PR2.

x1.reason: HIGH in the fix itself: roles.sql grants table-wide SELECT then revokes in separate autocommit statements, so a concurrent read-only session can see hidden columns mid-rerun. Fixed in the next commit and reviewed as its own slice.
x1.fix: Wrap roles.sql in one transaction (BEGIN ... COMMIT).

x2.reason: Same defect as recheck r1 (HAVING threshold cast).
x2.fix: Bind thresholds without narrowing casts; PR2 first task.

x3.reason: Same defect as recheck r2 (SQLite millisecond truncation).
